findings.summary: Attribution by records would be shown with records the test writes itself, not records Athena writes, so the 'attributed by the records' part and criterion 2 are not truly shown.
findings.evidence: In athena-core, GitLandingRecords / LandingRecords appear only in gh.rs (land_pr) and reconcile.rs (grep run on crates/athena-core/src). The plan's open question says the test 'may write [landing records] directly' for a locally landed commit and a declared intervention. Fix: Trace how an intervention and a records-only commit made after C0 get a landing record in production (reconcile, a manage.rs path, or none). If no path exists, add one inside the plan's scope. The lifecycle test must then produce all three commits and their records through Athena's own entry points (land_pr with a fake host, then reconcile, or the intervention command) and must not write landing records by hand. If some commit type truly cannot be attributed without new record writing, say so and narrow or split the job.

findings.summary: The criterion 3 command does not run all the tests the demonstration describes.
findings.evidence: The command is `cargo test --locked -p athena-core after_c0_readers_still_use_trailers_up_to_c0`, but the plan puts tests in both status.rs and auditor.rs, plus a strict-squash_text test in athena-git, which -p athena-core does not run. Fix: Name each test and give commands that run them all, e.g. a shared name prefix for the status and auditor tests, plus `-p athena-git` for the squash_text test.

findings.summary: Weakening a commit-time check is left as an open question, not decided.
findings.evidence: history.rs:161 runs invariant::check only for commits up to C0, so skipping it at commit time matches the history check. But it removes a commit-time safeguard, and the plan leaves that decision open. Fix: State the decision in docs/decisions.md under D111. Add a gate test showing that, after C0, the secrets, content and jobs checks still refuse a bad commit.

summary: The plan is placed correctly, and every function it names exists in the snapshot: Committer::build_commit_in (commits.rs:150), commit_with_staged (manage.rs:407), gate() (gate lib.rs:313), attribution::cutover_state (attribution.rs:132), history::check_history (history.rs:39), legacy::check_attribution_with_legacy, gh::landed_commit (gh.rs:1223), Git::squash_text (git lib.rs:715), status trace and auditor read_changed_files. Removing trailers in the two commit-writing functions, keyed on the same Shown-cutover condition check_history uses, is a sound single-point design. Building the squash text from the landed commit (gh.rs:2171) means stripping the trailers there also carries through to PR squash merges. Using manage.rs and gate lib.rs is justified: the request's Files line names whole crates. So Athena's scope findings are minor at most. The main gap is criterion 1's "attributed by the records". In the snapshot, landing records are written only by the PR landing path and by reconcile (GitLandingRecords in gh.rs and reconcile.rs). The plan's open questions say the test "may write them directly" for a local landing and an intervention. A test that writes its own landing records would show the check passing on records the test made up, not that Athena attributes trailer-less commits. It would pass even if production never writes a record for an intervention or a records-only commit, and those commits would then be unattributed after C0. The plan needs to name the production path that writes these records, or add one, and use it in the test. A smaller issue is that the criterion 3 command does not run all the tests it describes.
